subject: NovaRetail SLO qualification & cost path-map
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Zhou <emma.zhou@novaretail.com>, Tom Chen <tom.chen@novaretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: NovaRetail SLO qualification & cost path-map

Hi Emma / Tom — great conversation today, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap and the concrete asks so we can size the pilot and recommend cost/perf levers.

Call notes (TL;DR):
- Target: P95 latency <= 140ms for single-turn product search calls; streaming for recommendation snippets (partial token latency target ~60–80ms first-byte).
- Expected steady QPS: 120 requests/sec peak (US region) with 20% headroom for holiday spikes.
- Typical request: 1.2k tokens input, 150 tokens output (avg).
- Hard constraints: no PII leaves their VPC during Private trial; request-level audit logs required.

Primary risks we flagged:
- Streaming throughput under concurrent sessions (they have UI with 600 concurrent users during promos).
- Cost sensitivity: want < 50% uplift vs their current cost target for same feature latency.

Suggested next steps from Redwood (action items):
1) Emma/Tom: share two weeks of anonymized qps/latency samples (CSV) and a sample 50 queries representative of worst-case prompts — we referenced novaretail_qps_samples.csv.
2) Redwood: produce a short pilot proposal with: expected infra footprint, recommended batching/caching/quantization profile, and two model-variant paths (low-latency variant + cost-optimized variant). Target delivery: 48 business hours after receiving samples.
3) Security: we'll include a Private trial checklist and SOC2 artifacts; Karthik will own the network/KMS notes.

Early tradeoffs we discussed (we'll formalize in the matrix):
- Continuous batching improves GPU utilization but can add 10–40ms to tail latency depending on arrival skew; we can bound this with adaptive max-wait timers.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated user context can cut per-request cost by ~30% for recommendation-heavy flows.
- Quantization (int8 / 4-bit kernels) gives 2–3x cost improvement with small accuracy delta on reranker models; for generative snippets we recommend conservative int8 profiles and validation.
- Fall back to a ~6B model-variant for high tail-load periods to keep p95 within SLO with graceful quality fallback.

Attachments: we referenced a sample CSV and will send a short XLSX tradeoff matrix after you share samples.

Questions for you to unblock the pilot:
- Can you confirm the 600 concurrent active users assumption during promos, and whether all of them will use streaming UI at once?
- Any strict throughput caps on your end (load balancers, WAF) we should know about?

Thanks — I’ll wait for the CSV and sample prompts and will circulate the pilot plan ASAP.

—

Subject: Re: NovaRetail SLO qualification & cost path-map

Thanks Mina — sharing the files now (attached). A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 600 concurrent number is peak concurrent sessions on search pages; probably ~40% of them will hit the streaming recommendation panel. We can annotate the CSV with a flag.
- We can’t share raw user IDs; data team will anonymize and keep IPs masked. Is that sufficient for the pilot?
- For fallbacks: we prefer quality first on weekdays, but during flash sales we want latency-first (we can toggle via a feature flag).

I attached: novaretail_qps_samples.csv (hourly bins + sample request traces) and a short doc describing our streaming UX.

If you could include a small matrix that shows expected cost delta for: (a) continuous batching on, (b) caching on, (c) int8 quantization on — that'd be ideal. We want a one-page summary for the procurement team.

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: NovaRetail pilot plan draft

Mina / Ben — quick internal note while I build the pilot. I sketched a tradeoff matrix (attached) and proposed configuration:

1) Baseline (quality-priority):
- Model: rdx-7b-std (FP16)
- Quantization: none
- Batching: adaptive continuous (max-wait 8ms, max-batch 64)
- Caching: prefix KV cache enabled (TTL 15m)
- Expected P95: 110–130ms at 120 QPS; cost: baseline X

2) Cost-optimized (latency guardrails):
- Model: rdx-6b-quant (int8 kernels) for gen + rdx-7b-rerank (int8) for scoring
- Batching: more aggressive (max-wait 16ms, batch up to 128) with dynamic overflow to smaller variant
- Caching: aggressive (TTL 30m) for repeated contexts
- Expected P95: 130–160ms depending on arrival skew; cost: ~0.45X baseline

3) Flash-sale path (latency-first, graceful quality drop):
- Model: rdx-4b-fast (quantized) for most requests; fallback to 7b if quality threshold breach observed in A/B sampling
- Streaming: use small first-chunk tokenization + low-latency kernel; aim first-byte <= 70ms

Notes on validation: we should run a 24-hour replay using the provided CSV with two knobs toggled: caching on/off and batching windows at 8ms/16ms/32ms. That will give us an empirical p95 delta and GPU-hours estimate.

I attached the draft SLO_tradeoff_matrix.xlsx and a short runbook outline. Once Mina reviews, we can push the pilot proposal to NovaRetail.

—Karthik

Emma / Tom — thanks for the CSV, that was fast. Attached is the pilot summary (one-pager) and the tradeoff matrix Karthik built. High-level next steps and timeline:

1) Redwood to run 24-hour replay and sizing run (48 hours) — deliverable: expected P95/P99, GPU-hours estimate, and cost delta matrix.
2) Sync to review results (30m) — proposed: Fri 9/3 10:00am PT.
3) Security kick-off: we’ll send the Private trial checklist and SOC2 artifacts within 2 business days; Karthik will coordinate KMS notes with your infra contact.

Immediate asks for you:
- Approve the Friday slot or propose alternative.
- Confirm whether the feature-flag for sales-mode toggle exists and who we should talk to for coordination.

We’ll include two pilot configurations in the deliverable: quality-priority (lower batching, limited quant) and cost-optimized (aggressive quant + caching). If both look acceptable, procurement can pick the track or we can run an A/B style pilot.

Thanks — I’ll attach the pilot deliverable to HubSpot and share the Drive link.
